note: Backs Phase 2B of the recognition harness. Adjacency is COMPUTED, not generated: two regimes are neighbors when they share evidence clusters, so the scaffold becomes retrieval and its accuracy is auditable. Trigger conditions are keyed to the system attributes captured in Phase 1, so candidate regimes are derived mechanically from what the subject described. Everything produced from this file is still a CANDIDATE and still requires confirmation with a novel detail.

evidence_clusters.access_review: Periodic user access certification, joiner-mover-leaver, privileged access, segregation of duties
evidence_clusters.risk_assessment: Formal risk analysis, risk register, treatment plans, management acceptance
evidence_clusters.vendor_risk: Third-party assessments, security questionnaires, sub-processor lists, flow-down clauses
evidence_clusters.change_control: Approval gates, release management, emergency change handling, separation of duties in deploy
evidence_clusters.incident_response: IR plan, classification, notification decision, tabletop exercises, postmortems
evidence_clusters.crypto_key_mgmt: Encryption in transit and at rest, key rotation, HSM or KMS custody
evidence_clusters.logging_monitoring: Log integrity, retention, alerting, SIEM, audit trails
evidence_clusters.bcdr: Backup, restore testing, DR exercises, RTO and RPO definition
evidence_clusters.awareness_training: Role-based security training, phishing simulation, completion evidence
evidence_clusters.pen_test: Scoping, execution, remediation tracking, retest, scan cadence
evidence_clusters.asset_inventory: System and data inventory, classification, ownership
evidence_clusters.data_flow_mapping: Data flow diagrams, boundary definition, transfer mechanisms
evidence_clusters.retention_deletion: Retention schedules, deletion propagation, legal hold
evidence_clusters.subject_rights: Access, deletion, correction, portability, opt-out request handling
evidence_clusters.policy_governance: Policy set, ownership, annual review, exception process
evidence_clusters.control_narratives: Written control descriptions, evidence collection, auditor walkthroughs
evidence_clusters.continuous_monitoring: Ongoing control evidence, monthly reporting, POA and M discipline
evidence_clusters.customer_security_review: Customer security questionnaires, contract security exhibits, audit rights
evidence_clusters.accessibility_testing: WCAG conformance testing, VPAT, assistive technology validation
evidence_clusters.validation_qualification: IQ, OQ, PQ, validation protocols and reports

regimes.name: SOC 2 Type II
regimes.why: Multi-tenant service handling customer data, sold to enterprise buyers who demand an independent report.
regimes.observable: A CPA firm auditor, a defined audit period, control narratives, an evidence request list, a bridge letter between periods.
role_signals: negotiated a qualified opinion or an exception

regimes.name: ISO/IEC 27001
regimes.why: International customers or a procurement process that treats certification as table stakes.
regimes.observable: An accredited certification body, a Statement of Applicability, internal audit, management review minutes, a three-year cycle with surveillance audits.

regimes.name: HIPAA Security Rule
regimes.why: Electronic PHI handled as a covered entity or business associate.
regimes.observable: A signed BAA, a documented risk analysis, workforce sanction policy, breach classification decisions.
role_signals: decided whether an event was a reportable breach
regimes.silent_form: Very often done without anyone saying HIPAA out loud: if PHI was in the system and there was a customer contract, a BAA existed and its obligations attached.

regimes.name: HIPAA Privacy Rule
regimes.why: Use and disclosure of PHI, not just its protection.
regimes.observable: Minimum-necessary access design, notice of privacy practices, accounting of disclosures, patient access requests.
role_signals: built patient record access or amendment flows

regimes.name: HITRUST CSF
regimes.why: Healthcare buyers who want one assessment that maps across HIPAA, ISO and NIST.
regimes.observable: An authorized external assessor, MyCSF, a scored r2 assessment, a corrective action plan.
role_signals: mapped existing SOC 2 evidence into the CSF

regimes.name: PCI DSS
regimes.why: Cardholder data stored, processed or transmitted.
regimes.observable: A QSA or a self-assessment questionnaire, quarterly ASV scans, segmentation testing, a cardholder data environment boundary.
role_signals: made the tokenization or scope-reduction decision
chose SAQ type or drove a ROC

regimes.name: Card scheme and acquirer rules
regimes.why: Card acceptance pulls in the acquirer agreement and network rules alongside PCI DSS.
regimes.observable: Acquirer correspondence, chargeback ratio monitoring, network compliance programs, BIN sponsorship.

regimes.name: NACHA Operating Rules
regimes.why: ACH origination or receipt.
regimes.observable: ODFI agreement, return code handling, re-presentment limits, account validation for WEB debits, an annual rules compliance audit.

regimes.name: BSA / AML and sanctions screening
regimes.why: Money movement of any kind at a regulated institution or its technology provider.
regimes.observable: KYC and CIP flows, OFAC screening, SAR referral paths, transaction monitoring rules and tuning.
role_signals: tuned monitoring rules against false positives

regimes.name: FedRAMP
regimes.why: Cloud service offered to federal agencies.
regimes.observable: A 3PAO, an SSP, a control baseline at Low, Moderate or High, a POA&M, monthly continuous monitoring deliverables, an agency or program authorization.
role_signals: walked a control from requirement to implemented capability
tied a payment or launch gate to the authorization date

regimes.name: FISMA / NIST RMF
regimes.why: Federal information systems, whether agency-run or contractor-operated.
regimes.observable: An ATO letter, a system categorization, annual assessment, an authorizing official.
role_signals: worked to an authorizing official's conditions

regimes.name: NIST SP 800-171 / DFARS 252.204-7012
regimes.why: Controlled Unclassified Information on a defense contract or its supply chain.
regimes.observable: An SSP, a POA&M, an SPRS score, incident reporting to DoD within 72 hours, flow-down to subcontractors.
role_signals: computed or defended an SPRS score

regimes.name: CMMC
regimes.why: DoD contracts requiring assessed rather than self-attested 800-171 implementation.
regimes.observable: A C3PAO assessment, a level determination, an affirming official.
role_signals: prepared for or sat through a C3PAO assessment
scoped an enclave to reduce assessment surface

regimes.name: ITAR / EAR export control
regimes.why: Defense articles, technical data, or controlled technology, including access by non-US persons.
regimes.observable: US-persons-only access controls, deemed-export analysis, an empowered official, technology control plan.
role_signals: handled a deemed export question for an offshore team

regimes.name: NISPOM / classified processing
regimes.why: Classified information on cleared facilities or systems.
regimes.observable: An FSO, a facility clearance, accreditation of the processing environment, personnel clearances.
role_signals: held a clearance tied to the role
regimes.caution: Frequently subject to disclosure limits. Capture the fact, mark the limit, render generically.

regimes.name: GDPR
regimes.why: Personal data of people in the EU, regardless of where the company sits.
regimes.observable: Records of processing under Article 30, DPIAs, a DPA with customers, sub-processor lists and notice, SCCs or an adequacy basis for transfers, a 72-hour supervisory notification clock.
role_signals: built deletion propagation across systems and backups

regimes.name: CCPA / CPRA
regimes.why: Personal information of California residents at a business meeting the thresholds.
regimes.observable: Opt-out of sale or sharing, service-provider contract terms, verified consumer requests, a privacy policy with disclosure categories.
role_signals: built the request intake and verification flow

regimes.name: State breach notification laws
regimes.why: Personal information about residents of essentially any US state.
regimes.observable: A notification decision matrix by state, attorney-general notice thresholds, timing obligations that differ by jurisdiction.
role_signals: ran the multi-state notification analysis for an incident

regimes.name: GLBA Safeguards Rule
regimes.why: Customer financial information at a financial institution or a covered non-bank.
regimes.observable: A named qualified individual, a written risk assessment, MFA, encryption requirements, an annual report to the board.
role_signals: was the qualified individual or briefed them

regimes.name: FFIEC examination expectations
regimes.why: Banks and credit unions, and the technology providers examined alongside them.
regimes.observable: Examiner requests, the IT handbooks, third-party risk expectations, findings and matters requiring attention.

regimes.name: NYDFS Part 500
regimes.why: Financial services licensed in New York.
regimes.observable: A CISO report to the board, annual certification of compliance, 72-hour incident notice, MFA mandates.
role_signals: signed or supported the annual certification

regimes.name: Sarbanes-Oxley ITGC
regimes.why: A public company, or a company preparing for one, with systems touching financial reporting.
regimes.observable: Scoped in-scope applications, external auditor testing, quarterly control evidence, deficiency and material weakness language.
role_signals: owned segregation of duties in a financial system
remediated a control deficiency before year-end

regimes.name: SEC cybersecurity disclosure
regimes.why: Public issuers must disclose material cybersecurity incidents and describe risk management annually.
regimes.observable: A materiality determination process, 8-K timing discipline, annual risk-management and governance disclosure.
role_signals: provided input to the annual disclosure

regimes.name: DORA
regimes.why: EU financial entities and their critical ICT providers.
regimes.observable: A register of information on ICT third parties, incident classification and reporting, threat-led penetration testing, contractual requirements on providers.
role_signals: renegotiated provider contracts for the required clauses

regimes.name: NIS2
regimes.why: Essential or important entities operating in the EU.
regimes.observable: Early warning within 24 hours, incident notification, management accountability, supply chain security measures.

regimes.name: 21 CFR Part 11
regimes.why: Electronic records and signatures in an FDA-regulated context.
regimes.observable: Validation protocols and reports, audit trails that cannot be disabled, electronic signature binding, change control tied to validation state.
role_signals: kept a system in a validated state through a release

regimes.name: FERPA
regimes.why: Education records at an institution or its service provider.
regimes.observable: School official exception language in contracts, directory information handling, parent and student access rights.
role_signals: built role-based access to student records

regimes.name: COPPA
regimes.why: Personal information from children under 13.
regimes.observable: Verifiable parental consent flows, age gating, retention limits, restrictions on behavioral advertising.
role_signals: implemented age gating or parental consent

regimes.name: BIPA and state biometric laws
regimes.why: Biometric identifiers collected from residents of Illinois and similar states.
regimes.observable: Written consent before collection, a published retention and destruction schedule, a prohibition on sale.

regimes.name: Section 508 / WCAG
regimes.why: Software sold to federal or state government, and increasingly to enterprises with accessibility policies.
regimes.observable: A VPAT or Accessibility Conformance Report, assistive technology testing, remediation backlogs tied to procurement.
role_signals: made an accessibility remediation a release gate

regimes.name: FCC accessibility and 911 obligations
regimes.why: Advanced communications services and interconnected voice.
regimes.observable: CVAA recordkeeping certifications, E911 or NG911 location and routing obligations, interoperability testing, agency reporting.
role_signals: filed or supported an FCC certification

regimes.name: StateRAMP
regimes.why: Cloud services sold to state and local government.
regimes.observable: A StateRAMP authorization package, a 3PAO, continuous monitoring against a state program.
role_signals: reused a FedRAMP package for a state authorization

regimes.name: EU AI Act
regimes.why: AI systems placed on the EU market, with obligations scaled to risk tier.
regimes.observable: Risk classification of the system, technical documentation, transparency notices, human oversight design, logging of system operation.
role_signals: built the human oversight or transparency layer
